paper_title: Production of dark matter axions from collapse of string-wall systems
coupling_convention: f_a in GeV (x-axis); m_a in eV (y-axis, derived from f_a via cosmological relation)
notes: Paper presents field-theoretic lattice simulations of axion production from domain wall collapse in the early universe. The main result is a cosmological upper bound on the axion decay constant f_a derived from requiring that the total relic abundance (from vacuum misalignment, string decay, and domain wall decay) does not exceed observed cold dark matter density. The paper concludes f_a ≲ (2.0–3.8)×10^10 GeV (Eq. 96), combined with astrophysical lower bound f_a ≳ 10^9 GeV, constraining the 'classical axion window' to f_a ≃ 10^9–10^10 GeV, corresponding to m_a ≃ 10^−3–10^−2 eV. This is a mass-independent (or rather, mass-dependent via QCD relation) cosmological bound on f_a. The coupling_type AxionMass is appropriate because the paper's primary result is on the f_a–m_a plane (via the cosmological relic abundance calculation), not on a direct coupling constant like g_agamma. The data_points encode the allowed region: f_a ranges from ~10^9 to ~10^10 GeV; the corresponding m_a values follow from the QCD axion relation m_a ≃ (0.6 meV) × (10^12 GeV / f_a). For the upper bound f_a ≲ 3.8×10^10 GeV, m_a ≳ 1.6×10^−3 eV; for the lower bound f_a ≳ 10^9 GeV, m_a ≲ 6×10^−2 eV. The two-point representation [[1e9, 1e10], [1e10, 1e10]] marks the horizontal exclusion boundary at f_a ≃ 10^10 GeV (the geometric mean of the range).
